title: HTML, CSS & JavaScript Fundamentals Assessment
description: Comprehensive assessment covering semantic markup, CSS Flexbox/Grid, and modern JavaScript ES6+ features.

questions.question: Which CSS property is used to align flex items along the cross-axis of a flex container?
questions.explanation: 'align-items' controls alignment along the cross-axis, whereas 'justify-content' aligns items along the main-axis.

questions.question: What will be the output of `typeof null` in standard JavaScript?
questions.explanation: In JavaScript, 'typeof null' returns 'object' due to a historical legacy implementation quirk in the language.

questions.question: Explain the difference between synchronous and asynchronous execution in JavaScript, and provide an example of when asynchronous code is essential.
questions.explanation: Criteria: 1) Defines synchronous execution (blocking, executed sequentially line-by-line). 2) Defines asynchronous execution (non-blocking, handled via Event Loop / Microtask queue). 3) Provides a concrete scenario such as network HTTP requests (fetch API), file I/O, or database queries.

questions.question: Write a JavaScript function named `filterEvenNumbers` that accepts an array of numbers and returns a new array containing only the positive even integers using the `.filter()` method.

title: Python Data Structures & Operations Quiz
description: Evaluate understanding of lists, dictionaries, tuples, sets, list comprehensions, and basic Pandas DataFrames.

questions.question: Which built-in Python data structure is immutable and preserves order?
questions.explanation: Tuples in Python are immutable sequences; once created, their elements cannot be modified, added, or removed.

questions.question: Given a dictionary `scores = {'Alice': 85, 'Bob': 92, 'Charlie': 78}`, write a dictionary comprehension that creates a new dictionary containing only students who scored 80 or above.
questions.explanation:
Solution:
```python
passed = {name: score for name, score in scores.items() if score >= 80}
```
